narrative.summary: NATO adopted its first Artificial Intelligence Strategy in October 2021, setting six Principles of Responsible Use of AI in Defence, and published a revised AI strategy in July 2024 after its endorsement at the Washington Summit. In October 2022 Defence Ministers approved an Autonomy Implementation Plan and established the Data and Artificial Intelligence Review Board to put the principles into practice. NATO publishes public summaries of these texts. In January 2026 NATO published an Alliance Digital Strategy to 2035 whose data and AI principle calls for the wide use of AI in NATO digital services with consideration for the Principles of Responsible Use.

instruments.official_title: Summary of the NATO Artificial Intelligence Strategy
instruments.english_title: Summary of the NATO Artificial Intelligence Strategy
instruments.summary: Public summary of NATO's first AI strategy for defence and security. It aims to encourage responsible development and use of AI by Allies, accelerate adoption, protect AI technologies and innovation capacity, and counter malicious use of AI. It sets six Principles of Responsible Use of AI in Defence: lawfulness; responsibility and accountability; explainability and traceability; reliability; governability; and bias mitigation.
instruments.current_status: Published by NATO as an official text on 22 October 2021.
instruments.evidence_reference: Printed date 22 October 2021 on NATO 'Official texts' page (read 2026-10-21). Endorsement by Defence Ministers stated on NATO topic page 'Emerging and disruptive technologies' (topics_184303). Old URL official_texts_187617.htm still carries the principles text. Lifecycle could be 'superseded' by the 2024 revision; NATO describes the 2024 text as a revision building on the 2021 principles, so kept as adopted. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, 22 Oct 2021 date, four aims and six principles confirmed.; The page does not say Defence Ministers endorsed the strategy, nor mention the 2024 revision.

instruments.official_title: Summary of NATO's revised Artificial Intelligence (AI) strategy
instruments.english_title: Summary of NATO's revised Artificial Intelligence (AI) strategy
instruments.summary: Updates NATO's 2021 AI strategy. It has four aims: lead by example in responsible AI, accelerate adoption and interoperability, protect AI technologies and manage their risks while preserving innovation, and safeguard against adversarial use of AI. It sets nine outcomes covering use cases, integration through defence planning, an AI-ready workforce, standards and review tools, understanding of risks, testing, evaluation, verification and validation, interoperability, shaping international norms, and convergence with other emerging technologies.
instruments.current_status: Published by NATO as an official text on 10 July 2024; it revises the 2021 AI Strategy.
instruments.evidence_reference: Printed date 10 July 2024 (read 2026-10-21). Endorsement by Allied Leaders at Washington Summit from NATO topic page topics_184303. Old URL official_texts_227237.htm. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, 10 July 2024 date, four aims and outcomes confirmed.; The page does not say Allied Leaders endorsed the strategy at the Washington Summit; generative/frontier AI and AI-enabled disinformation are not mentioned in the page as fetched.

instruments.official_title: Summary of NATO's Autonomy Implementation Plan
instruments.english_title: Summary of NATO's Autonomy Implementation Plan
instruments.summary: Public summary of NATO's plan for developing and using autonomous systems in defence. It sets seven desired outcomes, including a shared understanding of autonomy, interoperability, common standards, exercises, protection against autonomy-related threats and public trust, applies NATO's Principles of Responsible Use of AI to AI-enabled autonomous systems, and refers to the 2019 CCW guiding principles on lethal autonomous weapons.
instruments.current_status: Published by NATO as an official text on 13 October 2022.
instruments.evidence_reference: Printed date 13 October 2022 (read 2026-10-21). Approval by Defence Ministers on 13 October 2022 from NATO news item news_208342. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, 13 Oct 2022 date, seven outcomes, PRUs and 2019 CCW principles confirmed.; Page does not say Defence Ministers approved the plan.

instruments.official_title: NATO's Data and Artificial Intelligence Review Board
instruments.english_title: NATO's Data and Artificial Intelligence Review Board
instruments.summary: Official text setting out the purpose and functions of the Data and Artificial Intelligence Review Board (DARB), NATO's forum and focal point for governing responsible AI development and use. The Board is to turn the six Principles of Responsible Use into practical toolkits and a responsible AI certification standard, guide implementation across the NATO Enterprise, and support Allies who voluntarily apply these tools nationally. Each Ally nominates one representative.
instruments.current_status: Published by NATO as an official text on 13 October 2022. Allies may use the Board's toolkits voluntarily in national efforts.
instruments.evidence_reference: Printed date 13 October 2022 (read 2026-10-21); listed under NATO 'Official texts'. legal_status chosen as nonbinding_guidance (governance framework); could alternatively be government-governance strategy. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, date, functions, voluntary national use and one nominee per Ally confirmed.; Page does not say Defence Ministers agreed to establish the Board.

instruments.summary: NATO's Alliance-wide digital strategy, building on the 2022 Digital Transformation Vision and extending its trajectory to 2035, with five strategic objectives: mission-driven digital transformation, interoperable and secure-by-design infrastructure, data-centric operations, accelerated innovation adoption and digital workforce enablement; it aims to fully enable multi-domain operations by 2030. Its 'Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Ecosystem' principle states that the wide use of AI technology in NATO digital services shall be promoted and accelerated with consideration for the NATO-agreed Principles of Responsible Use, and expects inference AI to improve warfighters' situational awareness. It also requires training on personnel interaction with AI-enabled systems and tracks AI adoption gains as a performance indicator; the Digital Policy Committee is responsible for updating it.
instruments.current_status: Published by NATO as an official text dated 13 January 2026 (full text with an appendix on the Digital Regulatory Framework). The text does not state which NATO body approved it or when.
instruments.evidence_reference: Deep sweep 2026-11-08: WebFetch of the nato.int official-texts page (full text, two fetches). Title 'Alliance Digital Strategy'; date '13 January 2026'. Principle para. 11 heading 'Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Ecosystem'; quotes: 'The wide use of AI technology in NATO digital services shall be promoted and accelerated', 'with consideration for the NATO-agreed Principles of Responsible Use', 'the deployment of inference AI solutions will improve the warfighter's situational awareness'. No approving body stated. Not found in NATO.json by title or URL. | Independent check: WebFetch https://www.nato.int/en/about-us/official-texts-and-resources/official-texts/2026/01/13/alliance-digital-strategy: title 'Alliance Digital Strategy'; date '13 January 2026'; objectives paras 18-22 'Mission-Driven Digital Transformation ... Digital Workforce Enablement'; para 11 'The wide use of AI technology in NATO digital services shall be promoted and accelerated'; para 15 'personnel interaction with AI-enabled systems'; para 25 KPI 'operational effectiveness gains attributed to AI adoption'; para 18 'fully enable MDO by 2030'. No approving body stated; DPC named as responsible for updates. Not in NATO.json (4 records: 2021/2024 AI strategy summaries, Autonomy Implementation Plan, DARB); DT Vision 2022 is only a lead. | Note: Qualifies (official full text, AI principle with directive language). Summary's objective names did not match the text, and the 'tactical edge' wording was not confirmed; rewritten from the text. Added 'sectoral' (defence) per NATO.json convention. leads.note: Covers EDTs broadly; no official text link found on NATO pages read.

leads.title: NATO Data Exploitation Framework Policy (2021) and Digital Transformation Vision (October 2022)
leads.note: Data and digital texts referred to in news; AI not the main subject and no published summary located. Update 2026-11-08: an official 'Summary of NATO's Data Exploitation Framework Policy' (23 November 2022) is published on nato.int and is now the link here (previous news link: https://www.nato.int/en/news-and-events/articles/news/2022/10/13/nato-allies-take-further-steps-towards-responsible-use-of-ai-data-autonomy-and-digital-transformation). AI appears only in its footnote 2 (principles drawn from the NATO AI Strategy; supports compliance with the Principles of Responsible Use), so it stays outside the scope test. The Alliance Digital Strategy (13 January 2026), now recorded, builds on the 2022 Digital Transformation Vision.

leads.title: Washington Summit Declaration (10 July 2024) and later summit declarations
leads.note: Mention AI only in passing (endorsement of revised AI strategy). The Ankara Summit Declaration (8 July 2026, nato.int official texts) mentions AI only in passing ('adopting powerful AI models'), so it stays a lead.

leads.title: Data Strategy for the Alliance (approved by the North Atlantic Council February 2025; published 5 May 2025)
leads.note: Official text on nato.int. A data strategy in which AI appears only in passing (AI and machine learning models within the Alliance data sharing ecosystem; a domain ontology that supports the effective use of AI; a footnote citing NATO's AI Strategy). AI is not one of its pillars, so it is outside the scope test.

leads.title: Data Quality Framework for the Alliance (29 August 2025)
leads.note: Official text on nato.int. Data-quality framework with seven quality dimensions; several AI references (data for training AI-enabled tools, data quality in machine-learning operations for responsible AI toolkits, 'ensure responsible AI adoption through relevant assessments and toolkits'). AI is a purpose rather than the subject and the approving body is not stated. Borderline: could become a risk-assurance record if data-for-AI frameworks are brought into scope.

leads.title: NATO's Digital Transformation Implementation Strategy 2.0 (26 May 2026) and Summary of NATO's Rapid Adoption Action Plan (25 June 2025)
leads.note: Both official texts on nato.int were read; neither mentions artificial intelligence (the Digital Transformation Implementation Strategy 2.0 refers only to emerging technologies; the Rapid Adoption Action Plan summary to emerging and disruptive technologies and the Principles of Responsible Use). Outside the scope test; listed so they are not re-checked. Rapid Adoption Action Plan summary: https://www.nato.int/fr/about-us/official-texts-and-resources/official-texts/2025/06/25/summary-of-natos-rapid-adoption-action-plan?selectedLocale=en
